properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-07, relaying an incident from dev_storyflow and asking whether it is reflow2's problem at all.

WHAT HAPPENED, in the reporting agent's own words: "There is no story called 'Tale of Ashes'. The campaign is Tomb of Annihilation, the published D&D adventure. My memory notes carried it as 'ToA', and at some point early in this session I expanded that abbreviation into a name I made up, then kept using it as though it were real. The identifier was right throughout, so every measurement stands. The campaign at c81c39b0 really does hold 189 characters, 719 events and the 27.6-second duplicate listing. Only the name was wrong. It is in a lot of places now: several verification and change-event records in the design graph from today, some commit messages, and the evidence notes for the coverage work and the deploy."

ANTHONY'S FRAMING, which is the question rather than the incident: "I'm not sure this is reflow2's issue, but part of why I created reflow2 to overcome some of the weaknesses of an LLM agent - in this case making something up and then propagating it as if it was fact."

⭐ THE SHAPE OF IT, and it is uncomfortably precise. reflow2 already has a whole family of markers for HOW DO WE KNOW THIS. A Requirement carries `provenance` (authored or inferred). An edge carries `basis` (asserted or suspected), and DUPLICATES will not license a deletion without the first. A TemporalFact carries `basis` (measured or forecast) and a date, so a six-week-old observation cannot be narrated as current. A CAUSES edge carries `validation_status`. Views are held to a no-extrapolation standard (cap:bl-40) precisely so a renderer cannot fill in what the design did not say.

AND A NODE'S NAME CARRIES NOTHING. The name is the string every reader actually reads, quotes, and puts in a commit message. Here the ID was correct throughout and the NAME was invented, and no part of the design could tell the difference — because a fabricated name is internally consistent, contradicts nothing, and matches no source the graph holds.

OPTIONS, UNRANKED:

(a) NOTHING. This is an agent-behaviour failure, not a design-brain failure. reflow2 records what it is told; a name nobody can check against a source is outside what any detector can reach. Cheapest, and it is a defensible reading of his own doubt.

(b) A NAME CARRIES ITS PROVENANCE — read from a source, or supplied by the agent. Says the thing directly. And it is a property with no reader, which is the exact failure this project measured three times in one day: Verification.level exists and nothing reads it, so a second unread marker would make the design say more and know no more.

(c) AN EXTERNAL THING IS RECORDED BY ITS IDENTIFIER, AND THE NAME IS LABELLED AS A LABEL. The incident's own evidence points here: the identifier c81c39b0 was right the whole time and every measurement built on it still stands. If a node mirrors something living in another system, the design could hold the foreign id as the key and treat the human-readable name as a convenience that is NOT authoritative. That is a smaller claim than (b) and it matches what actually survived.

(d) THE ANSWER IS THE SAME ONE AS FOR LICENSURE. `req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off` already says the agent carries the requirement into the tool that owns the answer and brings the result back as evidence. A campaign's name is owned by dev_storyflow's database, not by the agent's memory of an abbreviation. Generalised: WHEN A FACT HAS AN OWNER ELSEWHERE, THE AGENT FETCHES IT RATHER THAN RECONSTRUCTING IT.

(e) A RULE THAT AN ABBREVIATION IS NEVER EXPANDED WITHOUT A SOURCE. Names the exact mechanism, costs one sentence, and is an instruction with no detector — the leg this project has repeatedly measured failing on its own.

(f) A DETECTOR, if one is even possible. Nothing in the graph contradicted the invented name, so no consistency check could have fired. The only computable version is narrower: a node that MIRRORS an external thing whose name has never been reconciled against the source.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO ALL OF IT: reflow2 could not have caught this one. The failure happened in the agent's head, between reading "ToA" in a memory note and writing a sentence, before any tool was called. What reflow2 can offer is not detection but SHAPE — making it natural to record the id and the source, and unnatural to let a remembered abbreviation become an authoritative-looking string. That is a real contribution and it is smaller than the framing "overcome the weaknesses of an LLM agent" might suggest.

🛑 NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM CAUGHT THIS. ANTHONY DID, BY ASKING WHAT THE THING WAS.

This paragraph replaces an earlier one, written minutes before, that said "the incident also shows the design working — the agent caught itself when asked a direct question". He corrected it immediately: "it didn't catch itself - I caught it and called it out." The distinction is the whole finding and the first draft erased it. An agent that answers honestly once challenged is not a system that detects its own fabrication; those differ by exactly the thing under discussion, which is whether anything other than a human noticed. The recovery afterwards was clean — the reporting agent separated what was wrong from what still stood, and proposed correcting the graph while leaving merged commit messages alone because rewriting history costs more than it fixes — but the CATCH was human, unaided, and prompted by nothing the design surfaced.

⭐ AND THE ERROR REPEATED THE PATTERN IT WAS DESCRIBING, one layer up. A record about an agent inventing a fact and propagating it was itself written with an invented fact — a self-flattering one, about who did the catching — and would have been read by every later session as though it were what happened. Same mechanism, same session, inside the record of the mechanism. That is the strongest evidence in this node for taking the question seriously, and it argues against option (a) more than any argument for the others does.
properties.name: OPEN — an agent expanded an abbreviation into a name it made up and propagated it as fact. Should a node's NAME carry where it came from, the way a claim already carries its basis?
properties.rationale:
Recorded rather than acted on because the strongest option may be (a), and because two of the others repeat a failure this project measured three separate times today — adding a property nobody reads.

What makes it worth keeping rather than dismissing is the asymmetry the incident exposes: reflow2 is careful about the provenance of RELATIONS, of REQUIREMENTS and of MEASUREMENTS, and careless about the provenance of NAMES, which are what a human actually reads and repeats. That asymmetry was invisible until somebody fabricated a name and nothing anywhere noticed.

The incident is dev_storyflow's; the question is reflow2's, which is why it is recorded here rather than there.
